_comment: Single source of truth for task-type SEMANTICS. The tag NAME still lives in plan.md task names ([Migrate] X); this file holds what the tag MEANS (routing + gate exemptions + when-to-use hint + optional executor workflow + optional tactical-refactor flag). Code reads this via track_state.task_profiles, not hardcoded Python sets. The SubagentStart hook injects TAG_VOCAB + each tag's when_to_use into spec-planner, and the leading-tag profile (+ workflow + refactor flag) into task-executor — so a project overlay flows end-to-end with zero plugin edits (mirrors verify-mode-profiles.json). Adding a task type = one row here; if it needs special executor behavior set `workflow` (the [Migrate] generalization), and if a whole class should get a tactical refactor pass set `refactor: true` (the [Refactor] generalization).

_fields.route: which dispatch category drives _classify_task: manual | explore | executor
_fields.tdd_exempt: true => task is exempt from the TDD (red/green/refactor) gate
_fields.coverage_exempt: true => task is exempt from the coverage (F2/F3) gate. Explore is tdd_exempt but NOT coverage_exempt: it produces no code, yet must not skip coverage accounting on adjacent changes.
_fields.when_to_use: one-line 'when to use this tag' hint injected into spec-planner at dispatch (the closed-set guidance, data-driven so a project overlay's tags get a hint too). Absent => no hint injected.
_fields.workflow: prompt-shaping prose the executor follows when this tag is the leading tag — mirrors verify-mode `protocol`. Absent => default TDD (Steps 3-8). Only [Migrate] carries one today; a project overlay may add a bespoke workflow for a project tag (the [Migrate] generalization).
_fields.refactor: true => the tactical refactorer (agents/refactorer.md) is dispatched once after this task succeeds (the §3.6c seam). Mirrors the [Migrate] workflow-field generalization: a whole class of tasks opts into tactical refactor via one row, zero plugin edits. The [Refactor] name marker and CONDUCTOR_TASK_REFACTOR=1 env remain as per-task / per-session escape hatches. Absent/false = no tactical refactor (the default; the inline mechanical Step 5 refactor still runs in-task).
_fields.signals: optional keyword list derive_task_tag(description) signal-matches against to ADVISORILY classify a tagless task description (free text -> tag). A project overlay tag with `signals` becomes selectable with zero code edits. Absent => derive_task_tag falls back to tokens lifted from `when_to_use` (weaker matching). derive_task_tag is advisory and fail-open to None (default TDD) on ambiguity — init-from-plan still hard-validates the final tag.

Explore.when_to_use: Investigation/analysis that produces NO code or file change — architecture mapping, dependency survey, codebase understanding before implementation. task-executor REFUSES it (reports FAILURE): route to explorer instead.

Docs.when_to_use: Markdown/docs ONLY — no code touched at all. Edits .md, never source.

Config.when_to_use: Edits .env/.yaml/.json config with NO business logic — keys/values, not behavior.

Chore.when_to_use: Dependencies, tooling, CI/CD, build scripts with NO feature code.

Manual.when_to_use: Requires a HUMAN — UI walkthrough, cross-browser check, staging deploy, accessibility audit, email-delivery confirmation. Auto-deferred in continuous mode.

Refactor.when_to_use: A task that should get a tactical refactor pass after success — extract duplication, reduce complexity in the task's own diff. NOT TDD/coverage-exempt: it still owes a working test (the mechanical Step 5 contract). The leading-tag [Refactor] is the declarative form; the inline [Refactor] name marker remains a per-task escape hatch for a task whose leading tag is something else (e.g. [Config] Refactor the env loader). Deliberately carries NO `signals` — [Refactor] is an opt-in, not a goal-detected tag (derive_task_tag must NOT auto-propose it for any description containing 'refactor', or every readability tweak would silently opt into the tactical refactorer).

Migrate.when_to_use: Framework/version migration, package rename, or major-dep bump where an EXISTING test suite is the safety net — the suite starts red, success is making it green, not writing a new failing test first.
Migrate.workflow:
A `[Migrate]` task inverts TDD: the existing suite's red state is the START, green is the GOAL. You are not writing a new failing test first; you are making the existing suite pass again. Routes to executor (wave-eligible when flat + deps-declared); loads ACs normally (the checkpoint's ac-tracer needs the trace; you commit real code).

- **No Step 3 (Red).** The suite's current failures ARE the red state — do not author a new failing test for the migration.
- **Step 4 (Green) is the whole task.** Run the suite via the digester (§4.5, `PURPOSE=coverage` read as "run the suite once"), fix the compile/runtime breaks (deprecated APIs, `javax→jakarta` renames, removed methods, renamed config keys) until green. Commit each fix `fix(migrate): …`; a behavior-preserving mass change may commit `refactor(migrate): …`. Both are **F2-exempt** — do not stage a contrived test to satisfy F2; the existing suite covers the behavior.
- **Step 5 (Refactor) stays.** A bounded, diff-scoped, behavior-preserving pass under green (e.g. consolidating the rename); skip near the §7.0 tripwire.
- **No Step 6 coverage gate.** Coverage is suspended for `[Migrate]` (behavior is preserved, not added) — do not invent tests to hit 80%.
- **Step 7/8 apply normally.** If the migration diverges from the recorded tech stack (new framework version), update `tech-stack.md` in Step 7.
- **Stop conditions:** suite green → `--status success` (the existing suite is your evidence); suite still red after exhausting the failure list → `--status failure` with the remaining failing tests in `--failure-reason` (the phase-checker treats an all-migration phase's red exit as a FAILED report, not a fix-and-retry trigger).
